questions.q: What does "composability" mean at the smart-contract level?
options: Protocols must sign a partnership agreement before integrating
Only government-approved protocols can interact with each other
Any contract can call any other contract's public functions, with no approval process needed
Each protocol requires a unique API key to be called by another contract
questions.explain: Composability is the mechanical fact that any contract's public functions are callable by any other contract — no partnership or approval layer sits between them.

questions.q: Why can a completely unrelated protocol accept an aToken as collateral with no custom integration work?
options: Because the lending protocol pays the other protocol a licensing fee
Because aTokens are not actually transferable
Because all DeFi protocols share one single codebase
Because the aToken is just an ordinary ERC-20 token, like any other token the second protocol already supports
questions.explain: An aToken follows the standard ERC-20 interface, so any protocol that already knows how to handle ERC-20 tokens can accept it without writing anything custom.

questions.q: In the flash loan example, what happens if step 3 (repaying the loan plus fee) fails?
options: The entire transaction reverts, as if none of the three steps ever happened
Only step 3 is undone; the borrowed funds and the arbitrage trade stand
The flash-loan pool absorbs the loss permanently
The borrower keeps the funds but loses access to the protocol
questions.explain: A flash loan transaction is atomic — if any step, including repayment, fails, the entire transaction reverts and no partial state remains.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what made the 2022 Mango Markets exploit possible?
options: A hardware failure at a cloud hosting provider
A manipulated price feed in one place created automatic exposure for every protocol that relied on it, all within one transaction
A government regulation shutting down the protocol
Mango Markets had no smart contracts at all
questions.explain: Composability means a weak oracle in one place becomes every composed protocol's problem automatically — exactly how the Mango Markets exploit propagated.

questions.q: What is the relationship between atomicity and composability, per this lesson?
options: Atomicity is unrelated to composability and is unique to flash loans
Composability prevents transactions from ever reverting
A flash loan's all-or-nothing behavior depends on composability — multiple protocol calls inside one transaction that either all succeed or all revert together
Atomic transactions can only ever call a single protocol
questions.explain: It's composability — contracts freely calling other contracts within one transaction — that makes a flash loan's atomic, all-or-nothing structure possible.
